title: Grateful Dead Live at Metropolitan Sports Center on 1973-10-23
lineage: Dat (Sony D8) -> VXPocket v2 -> Samplitude Professional v10.1 -> FLAC (2 Discs Audio / 2 Discs FLAC)

ai_review.summary: Lovely soundboard capture of an energetic 10/23/73 show with a smoking Let It Grow, epic Casey Jones and Keith’s front‑and‑center organ magic.
ai_review.review: The recording is a well‑balanced soundboard that, after a brief early level tweak, delivers clear instrument separation and even highlights Keith's unusually forward organ mix. Musically the concert shines in the second set – Let It Grow (with a killer Keith solo), an intense Casey Jones that has Phil “going nuts,” The Other One and Weather Report Suite – though the on‑stage fight after the first two sets dampened the third‑set momentum.

ai_rating.rationale: Consistently high reviewer stars (mostly 4–5), strong praise for both performance and recording; many detailed comments confirming a great show despite the fight incident.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Clear, lovely sounding board with early‑set level adjustments; Keith’s organ/electric piano unusually forward but adds character; overall crisp and listenable.

show_quality.setlist_flow: First set a bit rough on sound levels, second set strong and creative, third set aborted after a fight that shifted the energy; overall flow praised for improvisational jams and seamless transitions.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Pumped up on Mexicali Blues; leads extra‑inspired throughout, though sits back during parts of Let It Grow.
band_member_comments.Phil: “Going nuts” on Casey Jones, visibly upset by the audience fight; strong bass presence noted.
band_member_comments.Bob: Bobby (Weir) described as pumped up; his guitar and vocals sit a bit high in the mix but add to the excitement.
band_member_comments.Keys: Keith’s organ/electric piano is unusually front‑and‑center, shines on Let It Grow and during the early “Wang Dang Doodle” soundcheck jam.
band_member_comments.Drums: Bill (Mickey) jumped offstage to help break up a fight; drum jams highlighted as strong moments.
